why: Making the right read when you have the advantage.
say: Attack the defender — if they stop you, pass; if they don't, score.
how: Two offense from half court, one defender in the lane.
Ball handler attacks; partner runs wide.
Read the defender: pass or finish.

why: The classic advantage read; also teaches tandem defense.
say: Middle stops at the free-throw line, wings run wide and cut.
how: 3 offense vs 2 defenders in tandem.
Middle drives to the free-throw line.
Read: pass to a wing, or score.
cue: Defense: top stops the ball, bottom takes the first pass

st: Top stops ball, bottom takes the pass

why: Getting back is effort, not talent.
say: On the miss, sprint to the paint first, then find your player.
how: Players at the far free-throw line.
Coach yells 'Back!'
Sprint, touch the paint, turn and find a player.
h: Coach passes ahead to a cherry-picker.

why: Teaches everyone where to run in transition.
say: Rebound, outlet, wings sprint wide, trailer comes behind.
how: 5 players, no defense.
Rebound and outlet to the guard.
Wings sprint, big runs the middle, trailer follows; finish.

say: Whoever rebounds outlets to a wing — those three go the other way.
how: 3 offense vs 2 defenders; outlet players on both sides.
After the shot, rebounder and outlets attack the other way.
Shooter becomes a defender; continuous.

st: Outlet — three go the other way

why: The ball moves faster than any dribbler.
say: Wings sprint, guard pitches it ahead — no dribbling in the backcourt.
how: Guard with the ball, wings on both sides.
Wings sprint ahead; guard passes ahead.
Wing attacks and finishes.

why: Slowing a fast break when outnumbered.
say: Backpedal, stay in front, force the ball handler to pick it up.
how: Defender retreats facing the ball.
Ball handler attacks full speed.
Defender shades and forces a stop or pull-up.

why: Rebound, dribble up, long lead pass, full-speed layup — everyone circles the court nonstop.
say: Dribble up, hit the runner as they cut in at the free-throw line, then sprint the circle — you're next.
how: A line under each basket, a cone at each free-throw line. Start on the right side (right-hand layups).
Rebounder takes it out of the net and dribbles up a few steps.
Runner sprints up the sideline; at the free-throw line extended they cut in — that's when the long lead pass comes.
Runner lays it in and joins the line under that basket. Passer sprints around the far cone, out to the other sideline, and becomes the next runner coming back.
Everyone circles the court the same direction. After a few minutes, flip to the left side for left-hand layups.
e: Shorter pass: the runner starts at half court.
h: Team goal: count makes in 2 minutes — misses don't count.

st: 1 takes it out of the net and dribbles up; 2 sprints up the right side
2 cuts in at the free-throw line extended — 1 throws the long lead pass
3 takes it out of the net, 2 joins that line, 1 rounds the cone and out to the side
3 dribbles up; 1 sprints up the other sideline
1 cuts in at the free-throw line extended — long lead pass
Right-hand layup — 4 is the next rebounder. Keep circling.

why: Finish at full speed with someone chasing — and never give up on a play.
say: Ball handler, beat him to the rim. Defender, sprint and contest from behind — no fouls.
how: Ball handler starts at the free-throw line extended; defender starts on the baseline behind them.
On 'go', the ball handler pushes full court for a layup.
Defender sprints to contest from behind — chest away, hand up, no swiping down.
Switch roles coming back.
e: Give the ball handler a bigger head start.
h: Defender starts right beside the ball handler.

st: Push it full court — defender chases from behind

why: Teaches sprinting back, stopping the ball, and talking when the defense is outnumbered.
say: When I call your number, touch the baseline — everyone else sprints back, stops the ball, and finds a man.
how: Offense on the baseline, defense facing them at the free-throw line, coach with the ball.
Coach passes to an offensive player and calls a defender's number.
That defender touches the baseline, then sprints back — 4-on-3 until they get there.
Play it out live; rotate groups.
e: Call the number before the pass.

st: Coach passes to 2 and calls 'three!' — x3 touches the baseline
Offense pushes; the defense sprints back while x3 chases
Kick to the open player — x3 recovers

why: Score an advantage fast before a recovering defender gets back.
say: You're up 2-on-1, but a defender is chasing — make the right read, fast.
how: Two offense start at half court; one defender in the lane.
A second defender starts behind the offense at half court.
Offense attacks on 'go'; the trailer sprints back to help.
Score or stop, then the next group goes.
e: Trailer waits one second before chasing.
h: Trailer starts level with the offense.

st: Defender commits — pass before the trailer gets there
